parts.title: Countdown
parts.text: Ada, Mateo, and Suki had trained all year for the Junior Space Academy's simulated flight to a **lunar** base. Inside the cabin, Ada, the commander, checked every **gauge** on the control panel while Mateo, the engineer, tested the fuel lines one last time. Suki, the navigator, studied the **trajectory** glowing on her screen, the curved path the shuttle would follow. "Ten seconds," she announced. "Everything looks perfect."

parts.title: Into the Dark
parts.text: When the engines roared, their thrust began to **propel** the shuttle upward, and soon it was starting to **hurtle** toward the stars at astonishing speed. Behind them, Earth shrank to a blue marble. Ahead stretched the **void**, an enormous emptiness with no air and no sound. Suki pointed at glittering **cosmic** dust drifting past the window, and Mateo whistled at the **stellar** view of a thousand burning stars.

parts.title: Trouble Aboard
parts.text: Suddenly an alarm blared. A **malfunction** in the heating system made the cabin walls **radiate** heat, and sweat dripped down Mateo's forehead. He traced the problem to a damaged battery pack and decided to **eject** it into space before it overheated. Ada steadied the controls and recalculated the route so they could still make their **rendezvous** with the moon station on schedule. "Stay calm," she told the crew. "We have trained for this."

parts.title: Mission Complete
parts.text: The shuttle docked smoothly, and the crew floated into the station to cheers from their instructors. Later, as they wrote their report, Suki admitted that her hands had shaken. Ada replied that bravery is not the absence of fear but the choice to keep working through it. The friends agreed that teamwork had saved the mission.

definitions.meaning1: Having to do with the moon. Example: A lunar eclipse turned the moon a deep shade of red.

definitions.meaning1: Having to do with the universe beyond Earth. Example: Scientists study cosmic rays that travel across space.
definitions.meaning2: Vast or enormous in size or importance. Example: The flood was a disaster of cosmic proportions.
definitions.studentChallenge: Telescopes help us explore the ___ mysteries of distant galaxies.

definitions.meaning1: A completely empty space; nothingness. Example: Beyond the last planet lay a cold, silent void.
definitions.meaning2: Not legally valid or binding. Example: The torn contract was void and could not be enforced.
definitions.studentChallenge: When her best friend moved away, she felt an aching ___ in her life.

definitions.meaning1: To push or drive something forward with force. Example: Strong, steady kicks will propel a swimmer across the pool.
definitions.studentChallenge: Powerful rocket engines ___ a spacecraft away from Earth.

definitions.meaning1: To move very fast, often with great force. Example: The runaway sled began to hurtle down the icy slope.
definitions.studentChallenge: Asteroids can ___ through space at thousands of miles per hour.

definitions.meaning1: A failure to work properly. Example: A sudden malfunction in the engine forced the pilot to land early.
definitions.meaning2: To stop working properly. Example: If the alarm should malfunction, call the repair line.
definitions.studentChallenge: A computer ___ erased the astronaut's flight data.

definitions.meaning1: Having to do with stars. Example: The telescope gave the club a stellar view of a glowing cluster.
definitions.meaning2: Outstanding or excellent. Example: Her stellar performance in the play earned a standing ovation.
definitions.studentChallenge: The orchestra gave a ___ performance that thrilled the crowd.

definitions.meaning1: An instrument that measures something, such as fuel or pressure. Example: The pilot glanced at the fuel gauge and saw the needle near empty.
definitions.meaning2: To estimate or judge. Example: Teachers watch students' faces to gauge how well they understand.
definitions.studentChallenge: The needle on the pressure ___ jumped into the red zone.

definitions.meaning1: To send out heat, light, or energy in all directions. Example: A campfire will radiate warmth in every direction.
definitions.meaning2: To show a feeling strongly. Example: She seemed to radiate happiness as she crossed the finish line.
definitions.studentChallenge: The glowing sun will ___ heat across the desert.

definitions.meaning1: To force or throw out suddenly. Example: The old toaster will eject the bread when it finishes.
definitions.meaning2: To make someone leave. Example: The referee had to eject the player who started the fight.
definitions.studentChallenge: The pilot pulled a lever to ___ the broken part into space.

definitions.meaning1: A planned meeting at a set time and place. Example: The two ships planned a rendezvous above the planet.
definitions.meaning2: To meet at an agreed place. Example: The friends agreed to rendezvous at the library at noon.
definitions.studentChallenge: The scouts arranged a ___ at the old oak tree at dawn.

definitions.meaning1: The curved path of a moving object through the air or space. Example: The cannonball followed a high trajectory before it landed in the lake.
definitions.meaning2: The course of something's development over time. Example: After her big win, the runner's career followed an upward trajectory.
